title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page sits in the part of the 'équation des lacets' manuscript that analyses certain algebraic groups M_{ρ,σ} and M°_{ρ,σ}. They are built from tori T_ρ, a group N'_σ (a torus-normaliser-type group carrying a sign character ε_σ), a 'scalar' torus T_0, and the group SG (which behaves like SL_2). The previous page showed that R_{ρ,σ} := Ker(Θ̄) commutes with SG.

(102) records the resulting central-product presentation: 1 → μ_2 → R_{ρ,σ} × SG → M_{ρ,σ} → 1, with ε ↦ (ε, ε^{-1}) = (ε, ε) since ε² = 1. So M is (R × SG)/μ_2, the same pattern as GL_2 = (G_m × SL_2)/μ_2.

(103) is the analogous sequence for the connected or neutral variant M°. Grothendieck notes it was already envisaged 'timidly' in (78).

(104) then makes R_{ρ,σ} explicit, in the setting of p. 510.
- R consists of products (u, a, b)·f with u ∈ T_0, a ∈ T_ρ, b ∈ N'_σ, f ∈ SG.
- The conditions are det u = det b = ε' det a with ε' ∈ μ_2, and u·f = λ scalar. Since f ∈ SG, this forces λ² = det u.
- Because f = λu^{-1} is determined by (u, λ), R ≅ {(u, a, b, λ) : det u = det b = ε' det a = λ²}.
- Eliminating u (determined by the data) and keeping ε' gives {(a, b, λ, ε') : det b = ε' det a = λ²}.
- Since ε' = det b / det a is forced, the condition ε'² = 1 becomes (det a)² = (det b)². So R ≅ {(a, b, λ) : det b = λ², det a² = det b²}.
- In other words R ≅ ((T_ρ, δ_ρ²) ×_{G_m} (N'_σ, δ_σ²)) ×_{δ_σ, G_m, sq} G_m.

Writing T_{ρ,σ} := {(a, b) : δ_ρ(a)² = δ_σ(b)²} with χ = δ_σ, this is the cartesian square (105):
- R_{ρ,σ} → T_{ρ,σ}, with λ: R → G_m and χ: T_{ρ,σ} → G_m;
- bottom map G_m → G_m, λ ↦ λ².

So R is the Kummer double cover of T_{ρ,σ} obtained by pulling back the squaring map along the character χ. This yields the extension 1 → μ_2 → R → T_{ρ,σ} → 1 displayed on the next page as (106).

A struck-out (105') gives the analogous description of R°_{ρ,σ}: {(a, b, λ) : det a = det b = λ²} ⊂ T_ρ × T_σ × G_m, which is T°_{ρ,σ}.

Purpose: to describe all the groups R, SR, T^+, T^0 and their characters χ, ε_ρ, ε_σ purely in terms of the elementary data T_ρ, N'_σ, δ_ρ, δ_σ, ε_σ (listed as (107)–(108) on the next page). This is presumably in service of computing the symmetry groups attached to the loop-equation configurations.
errors: No genuine mathematical error found. The passage from (a, b, λ, ε') to (a, b, λ) is correct: ε' = det b/det a, and ε'² = 1 iff (det a)² = (det b)².
In (102) the kernel μ_2 embeds as (ε, ε^{-1}). The previous page had claimed (then struck out) R ∩ SG = 1, whereas exactness here needs R ∩ SG = μ_2. The struck-out claim was evidently corrected.
The notation in the final fibre-product formula of (104) is somewhat loose. Which maps are used (δ_ρ², δ_σ² for the first fibre product; δ_σ and squaring for the second) has to be inferred.

ideas.what: Central product presentation M = (R × SG)/μ_2 with antidiagonal μ_2
ideas.modern_name: central product / isogeny presentation (like GL_2 = (G_m × SL_2)/μ_2)

ideas.what: R as the pullback of the squaring isogeny G_m → G_m along a character χ of T_{ρ,σ}
ideas.modern_name: Kummer (μ_2-)torsor / double cover of a diagonalizable group via a character

ideas.what: Explicit description of R_{ρ,σ} as an iterated fibre product of tori and normaliser-type groups over G_m via determinants
ideas.modern_name: fibre products of group schemes over G_m

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine bookkeeping computation of a central extension and a Kummer-type pullback of tori within a larger unpublished project. The project as a whole may be of interest, but this page contains no new result or unexpected connection.
transcription_corrections: Line (102): the image shows (ε, ε^{*1}) with '‖ ε^{-1}' written underneath, i.e. the second component equals ε^{-1}. The transcription's annotation 'ε^{-1} = ε' is an interpretation, not what is written.
The number above R_{ρ,σ} in (102) reads '510' or '520'. The text body refers to 'la p. 510'.
Under (104) the domains are written 'ΓT_0 ΓT_ρ ΓN'_σ SG', and '(d'où λ² = det u)' is a marginal note, not part of the set condition.
In the third line of (104) the struck-out fragment is 'det b ... ∈ Γ μ_2', and the added condition reads 'det b = ε' det a = λ²'.
